g.text: Use psychometrics to estimate latent abilities
The metabench framework leverages psychometric techniques
(Hambleton & Swaminathan, 2013; Wang et al., 2023a) to estimate
the latent abilities captured by these benchmarks (Burnell et al.,
g.title: N12 [Method] (cites=3) The metabench framework leverages psychometric techniques (Hambleton & Swaminathan, 2013; Wang et al., 2023a) to estimate the latent abilities captured by these benchmarks (Burnell et al., 2023).

g.text: These estimates can reconstruct individual and total benchmark
scores with minimal error, and reveal a single underlying factor
that captures most of their variability.
g.title: N13 [Result] (cites=0) These estimates can reconstruct individual and total benchmark scores with minimal error, and reveal a single underlying factor that captures most of their variability.

g.text: New lens for LLM ability measurement
By refining how we measure the abilities of LLMs, metabench offers
a new lens through which we can understand and improve them.
g.title: N14 [Method] (cites=0) By refining how we measure the abilities of LLMs, metabench offers a new lens through which we can understand and improve them.

g.text: Practitioners can run their own models on this efficient and
highly informative benchmark, obtain approximated scores, and
compute an overall estimate of their models' general ability.
g.title: N15 [Method] (cites=0) Practitioners can run their own models on this efficient and highly informative benchmark, obtain approximated scores, and compute an overall estimate of their models' general ability.

g.text: Disjoint second version for repeat eval
We additionally offer a second, disjoint version of metabench for
users that intend to evaluate an LLM multiple times.
g.title: N16 [Method] (cites=0) We additionally offer a second, disjoint version of metabench for users that intend to evaluate an LLM multiple times.

g.title: N18 [Method] (cites=0) It is aimed for the open-source community and independent machine learning researchers with limited resources.

g.text: We use data from n > 5000 LLMs to identify the most informative
items of six benchmarks, ARC, GSM8K, HellaSwag, MMLU, TruthfulQA
and WinoGrande (with d = 28,632 items in total). From them we
distill a sparse benchmark, metabench, that has…
g.title: C1 [Contribution] (cites=0) We use data from n > 5000 LLMs to identify the most informative items of six benchmarks, ARC, GSM8K, HellaSwag, MMLU, TruthfulQA and WinoGrande (with d = 28,632 items in total). From them we distill a sparse benchmark, metabench, that has less than 3% of the original size of all six benchmarks combined.

g.text: This new sparse benchmark goes beyond point scores by yielding
estimators of the underlying benchmark-specific abilities.
g.title: C2 [Contribution] (cites=0) This new sparse benchmark goes beyond point scores by yielding estimators of the underlying benchmark-specific abilities.

g.title: C3 [Contribution: Finding 1] (cites=0) We show that these estimators (1) can be used to reconstruct each original individual benchmark score with, on average, 1.24% root mean square error (RMSE),
